transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith... I'm really only sitting here because my wife and, well, pretty much everybody else, they keep acting like I'm just imagining the whole thing. Like I'm making it all up in my head. But I know what I see. I'm an assembler, you know? I put things together for a living, I work with my hands. I know where things go and I know exactly where I leave my things. 

And I know for a fact that her relative has been coming into this house—my own house—just to get at me. I'll go out to the garage, and my tools... my tools don't just move themselves, doc. I'll leave a wrench right on the workbench, exactly where I need it for the next day, and suddenly it's kicked under the air compressor or shoved in the wrong drawer. It's deliberate. 

And it’s not just the garage, it's everything I try to do. Every single weekend, I make my fishing plans. I just want to go down to the lake and get a little peace and quiet, but every time, it gets spoiled. It never fails. My gear is messed with, or things are missing, and that doesn't just happen by accident every single weekend, you know? It’s been going on for months now. Months of this. And I can see it plain as day, even if my wife won't admit it. He’s been trying to take over my place. He wants to push me out, make me look crazy so I'll pack up and leave, and then he can just take over everything I've worked for. They told me I needed to come talk to a doctor about it, so here I am, but I'm telling you, I'm not the one who's doing anything wrong here.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I hear the normal things, right? The wind, the cars on the street, the floorboards creaking when the house settles. But voices? Like, people whispering in my ear when nobody's there? No, absolutely not. I'm not crazy, doc, no matter what my wife says. I don't hear things that aren't there. 

What I *do* hear is the very real sound of my back gate latch clicking when it shouldn't be. I hear that. And I hear the side door to the garage rattling, just a little bit, like someone's testing it to see if I forgot to lock the deadbolt. Which I never do, by the way. I check it three times before bed now. But as for voices in my head? No. The only voice I hear is my own, telling me I need to stay vigilant, because if I don't, who knows what he'll do next? He's sneaky, you see. He doesn't make a lot of noise. He doesn't come stomping around yelling. He's quiet. That's how he gets in and messes with my tools. He waits until I'm asleep or in the shower, and he slips in, silent as a mouse. So, no, I don't hear voices. I just hear the real sounds of a man trying to ruin my life, one moved wrench at a time.
Aside from these concerns, have you noticed any changes in your memory, your ability to focus, or any new physical health problems recently?

No, my memory is sharp as a tack, doc. I mean, it has to be, right? If I didn't remember exactly where I left my 3/8-inch socket, I wouldn't know when he moved it. I can tell you exactly where I put every single tool in that garage before I go to bed. I even started taking pictures with my phone, just to prove it to myself, and to my wife, though she won't even look at them. But my memory? It's perfect. Better than ever, honestly, because I have to pay so much attention to every little detail now. 

And my focus... well, I'm focused, alright. I'm focused on protecting my home. When I'm at work, sure, maybe my mind wanders a bit, but only because I'm thinking about what he might be doing while I'm not there. I'm putting parts together on the line, but in my head, I'm running through the checklist. Did I lock the side door? Did I check the latch on the gate? Did I leave the motion sensor light on? It's not that I can't concentrate on my job—I still do my job just fine, I've been doing it for thirty years—but it's just that there are more important things demanding my attention right now. You understand, right? When someone is actively trying to push you out of your own life, you have to stay focused on that. You can't just ignore it.

As for my physical health, I feel fine. I mean, I'm tired, obviously. I don't sleep as well as I used to because I'm always listening for those sounds I told you about. The gate, the door. I lie there in bed, and my heart starts pounding sometimes when I think I hear something, but that's just normal, isn't it? That's just what happens when you're under stress. But I don't have any new aches or pains, no headaches, nothing like that. My body is fine. It's just my life that's being messed with.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter supplements, or using any substances like alcohol or drugs?

No, doc, I don't take anything. I mean, my wife is always on me about taking a multivitamin or some fish oil, but I don't bother with any of that. Never have. I don't like putting things in my body if I don't know exactly what they're doing, you know? Especially now. With everything going on, I need my mind to be completely clear. I can't afford to be groggy or have some pill messing with my head. 

I've never been one for medications anyway. Even when I get a bad cold or a headache from staring at the assembly line all day, I just power through it. A glass of water and a good night's sleep—well, when I could get a good night's sleep—that's always been enough for me. I don't even take aspirin unless my back is really acting up from bending over the workbench, and even then, I try to avoid it. 

And as for alcohol... well, I used to enjoy a beer on the weekends. Just one or two, sitting out on the back porch after I finished mowing the lawn. It was a nice little routine. But I stopped doing that a few months ago. Ever since all this started with him sneaking around. I realized I couldn't risk having even one beer, because what if it dulls my senses? What if I'm sitting there, relaxed, and I miss the sound of the gate latch? Or what if I fall asleep too heavily and don't hear him by the garage? I have to be ready, doc. I have to be on my toes. So, no alcohol. Not a drop. 

And drugs? Absolutely not. Never touched the stuff in my life. I've worked at the same plant for thirty years, and they do random testing, you know. Not that I'd ever take anything anyway, but I've got a clean record. Always have. So, no, I'm not taking anything at all. Just trying to keep my wits about me, because if I don't, I'm the one who's going to lose everything.
